learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how the internet connects the world, the basics of computer networking, and the protocols that make it all work!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A computer network is a group of computers connected together to share resources (like printers or files). Types of networks include LAN (Local, like in a school), MAN (Metropolitan, across a city), and WAN (Wide, across the world, like the Internet).

Topology refers to the physical or logical layout of a network. Common types are Star (all connected to a central hub), Bus (all connected to a single main cable), and Ring (connected in a closed loop).
The Internet is the massive hardware network connecting millions of computers globally. The WWW (World Wide Web) is the collection of web pages and information that you access *using* the Internet.
Protocols are rules that computers use to talk to each other. TCP/IP breaks data into packets and routes them. HTTP/HTTPS is used for viewing web pages securely. SMTP is used for sending emails.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Find Your IP Address
fun_activity.instructions: Every device on the internet has a unique number called an IP Address, just like your home address! Go to google.com and search 'What is my IP'. The numbers you see (like 192.168.1.5) are your computer's internet identity!

exam_tips: 📌 Always know the full forms: LAN, WAN, MAN, HTTP, URL, ISP, and HTML.
📌 Difference between Web Browser (Software like Chrome to view pages) and Web Server (Hardware/Software that stores the websites) is highly tested.
📌 Star topology is the most commonly used topology today because if one cable fails, the rest of the network keeps working.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Internet is a 'network of networks'.
⭐ An ISP (Internet Service Provider) is a company like Jio or Airtel that provides you internet access.
⭐ A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) consists of a protocol (http), domain name (google.com), and sometimes a specific file path.
